title: Home Mortgage Loans: Number of Loans a Borrower May Hold
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Number of Loans a Borrower May Hold

Piedmont Crescent Bank allows one customer to hold more than one of its Home Mortgage Loans. Holding is limited in three ways, all measured on loans that are still open, and all read from the bank's own loan records for that customer rather than from the customer's account of what they hold.

## The rule

1. **Customer-wide limit.** A new mortgage application may be recorded for a customer only while the number of that customer's loans standing as applied, active, delinquent or in forbearance is less than 4.
2. **Program limit.** The number of such loans the customer already has in the program being applied for must likewise be less than the allowance that program sets for a single customer.
3. **Government-program limit.** One customer may have no more than a single FHA or VA loan outstanding at a time on a primary residence.

Loans that have been paid off and applications that ended as withdrawn are left out of every count above.

## What counts

| Loan status in the bank's records | Counted toward the limits |
|---|---|
| applied | yes |
| active | yes |
| delinquent | yes |
| in forbearance | yes |
| paid off | no |
| withdrawn | no |

## Decision table for the two numeric limits

The table shows only whether these counting limits stand in the way of recording a new application; other lending rules continue to apply on their own terms.

| Open loans across all programs | Open loans in the requested program | Effect of this rule |
|---|---|---|
| fewer than 4 | fewer than the program allowance | the counts do not prevent recording |
| fewer than 4 | at or above the program allowance | not recorded |
| 4 or more | any | not recorded |

## Worked cases (hypothetical holdings)

- *Case A.* A customer holds two active Conventional 30-Year Fixed Mortgage loans, one paid-off loan and one withdrawn application, and applies for another loan in the same program. Open loans overall: 2, which is fewer than 4. Open loans in the program: 2. Provided the program's own allowance is greater than 2, neither count prevents recording; if the allowance were 2, the program limit alone would stop it.
- *Case B.* A customer has one active loan, one delinquent loan, one loan in forbearance and one pending application, across any programs. That is 4 open loans, so a fifth application cannot be recorded, whichever program is requested.

The holdings in these cases are invented to show how the counting works.
